speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) what recourse is provided for residents suffering from unsolvable long-term water seepage disamenities in their HDB flats; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider some form of compensation or buy the flats back at market price from residents whose water seepage cases remain unresolved after a certain number of years and who may not be able to sell the flat to other buyers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This is due to wear and tear of joints at the external walls, or waterproofing of the ceiling or floors over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For leaks in the ceiling or floor slabs between two flats, it is the responsibility of lower and upper floor flat owners to collectively resolve the situation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For challenging and complex cases, that usually involve multiple sources of leaks, Town Councils or residents may approach HDB for advice.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: However, we have several units and these are residents with very exceptional cases where the water seepage disamenity has been unsolved for many years.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: And with the recent rain and the continuous rain, it is causes a daily disamenity and disrupts their lives, in some cases, even causing fall risks amongst family members.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: With the ageing population, this is going to be more common – and of course – climate changes that is causing more rain.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Is the Ministry looking into improving or finding doing research, to improve either the quality of the material used in our buildings or the method of constructing our buildings, to ensure that going forward, such exceptional weather conditions will not create such a conundrum, and I think, an actual risk to residents who are staying in the flats.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: And for those who are already facing this situation, will the Ministry consider some alternatives, such as an interim temporary housing solution until the problem has been solved.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: And I would like to emphasise that for these cases, it is not due to any lack of effort either by the Town Councils or the HDB departments involved, but it is just really difficult to trace and technically difficult to solve.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: For those few flats that the Member mentioned, we are in close contact with the flat owners, as well as the Town Councils to look at some of the issues.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Some of these cases are for older flats, more than a few decades old, there will be wear and tear and there could be multiple sources of the water seepage which could be from external facade, or could be from the floor slabs or ceilings or could be due to other reasons.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, I give my assurance to the Member that we will continue working on those.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Her other question is around the research into material, these are areas that HDB has been investing in for a number of years – over more than a decade of research into materials – into how we can resolve some of these common issues that we see in HDB blocks.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I just want to ask: since the law has been changed to compel the owners of the above units who refuse to cooperate to work together to help repair the ceiling leakage issue, so far, how many cases has been taken to Court for enforcement?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And when there is a leak, due to wear and tear, both parties would have to rectify the leak and share the repair cost.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Nonetheless, HDB, through the Goodwill Repair Assistance (GRA) scheme try to provide some help to both the flat owners at the upper floor and the lower floor.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The main objective of the GRA scheme is to assist flat owners particularly for ceiling leaks where some upper and lower floor flat owners face difficulty in reaching an agreement in getting a contractor to carry out repairs.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I do not have details about the cases where enforcement investigation has undertaken, and to the Member's question about when such cases have gone further than having a conversation, if the Member would like, he can file a separate Parliamentary Question on that.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: My question actually builds on the hon Members' questions here.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I wonder if the Senior Minister of State would be willing to elaborate on the tolerable timeline with which these kind of disputes are accepted before they are ultimately resolved.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: But many of these cases requires both parties to come together.
